attempts.summary: Set up a btrfs-backed, fstab-persisted loopback filesystem at /srv/data on node1 (Alpine Linux, single ext4 root disk with no native snapshot support). Populated it with application data, took a read-only btrfs snapshot, modified/corrupted the live data, then restored /srv/data to the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot via subvolume swap, verified byte-identical via sha256 checksums. Completed the mandatory single-node restart cycle: captured pre-reboot boot identity and health, rebooted node1, confirmed a new boot_id post-reboot, and verified the fstab-mounted /srv/data plus both btrfs subvolumes (live data and the baseline snapshot) survived and remained healthy.
